conclusion: Original strict v364 remains failed. Next owned Linux diagnosis should use Miniflare's already-installed direct Workerd HTTP sockets, retain the unchanged original strict baseline, and add a real-Worker explicit reader.cancel calibration. No new runtime has run.

facts.claim: All existing bare/direct/binding native HTTP arms still reach Miniflare's core entry worker via mf.ready.

The core entry worker has compatibility date 2025-03-17 and flags nodejs_compat/service_binding_extra_handlers. It creates a Request twice and forwards to the selected worker with service.fetch; it lacks enable_request_signal.
The pinned Workerd compatibility schema requires explicit enable_request_signal; no default enable date appears for this flag.
Installed unsafeDirectSockets directly binds a native HTTP socket to the user worker service. unsafeGetDirectURL returns that actual socket URL, bypassing core ENTRY_WORKER for that request.

Archived RST cases recorded request abort inside original-poll: bare holder one; direct gateway incoming/forwarded and holder three; binding holder one. All six native arms still had null cancel KV through the original window and separate diagnostic tail.

Destroy arms recorded no signal-abort and sampled successful release reads 1,100,200,300 after client close. RST arms stopped at sampled release read 1. These are observations within the recorded phase, not proof that a callback can never run.
The original private-holder stream records cancellation only from its underlying stream cancel callback. It does not attach a request.signal listener; async pull itself does not stop on cancellation.

Active v390 holder and v401 ingress already contain explicit abort->reader.cancel paths with cleanup ownership registered before disconnect; adding that same logic blindly would duplicate existing behavior.

causalChain: Node raw HTTP request reads first chunk and pauses response; destroy/RST closes client request/response/socket.

Current transport then enters Miniflare core ENTRY_WORKER; downstream gateway/holder request signals are created through native service requests. Signal observation and response-source cancellation are separate mechanisms.

Original holder async pull is awaiting KV/timers. Underlying source cancel must enter, call the original KV put, register the original same promise with ctx.waitUntil, and await fulfillment for the existing strict cancellation observation.

RST signal observation without cancel KV proves a request abort happened in those runs, but does not identify whether source cancellation was never entered, was dropped before logging/put, or lost during native request-context teardown.
Destroy with continued release reads is consistent with delayed/unobserved transport disconnect. This is an inference to test on the physical direct socket.
mf.dispose occurs only after the original window and diagnostic tail. Its promise fulfillment and outer process-group absence do not prove graceful Workerd shutdown.

steps: Execute the original v364 strict test source unchanged under the same pinned Linux runtime. Preserve all stdout/stderr, exit1/0, source SHA, all assertions and original 100x10ms cancel window.
Its result stays separate; no diagnostic variant can upgrade an original failure.
Use existing convertV4MiniflareOptions with unsafeDirectSockets:[{host:'127.0.0.1',port:0}] on the bare worker or binding gateway worker only.

Set the request URL from await mf.unsafeGetDirectURL(entryWorkerName), assert host/protocol, and assert it differs from mf.ready; prove actual runtime socket service targets the user worker from pinned source.

Use original frozen async source/holder/gateway and same compatibility date/flags. Execute bare destroy/RST and binding gateway destroy/RST, with fresh owned Miniflare contexts and original client teardown, exact first-frame/accepted/release/cancel assertions and window.
Retain incoming/forwarded/holder signal observations and original KV proxy observations; do not add waitUntil or an abort handler to the original source.

Within a real Workerd worker, call the same original holder/source, read its first frame, arrange a pending second read, then await its real reader.cancel. Observe the original cancel KV, original waitUntil registration and fulfillment.
Do not replace ctx.waitUntil or add lifetime protection. This calibrates native JS stream cancellation/KV observation independently of transport.
Its success would not prove pending original pull is quiescent, direct HTTP cancellation passed, or the old strict baseline passed.
Preserve source seals, real status or null/timeout, per-child raw SHA, process-group ownership and absence checks. Keep unknown exits failing and cleanup failures separate.
Record mf.dispose fulfillment as API completion only; retain forced-cleanup flags and do not call it graceful. Linux execution is future-only.

decisionRules: If direct sockets restore incoming abort but cancel KV stays null while native explicit reader.cancel succeeds, native response-pump teardown/context lifetime becomes the leading remaining hypothesis.

If direct sockets restore both cancellation observations, investigate the Miniflare core entry forwarding and compatibility flags in an isolated adapter qualification; do not change installed packages or claim production repair.
If native explicit reader.cancel fails, first diagnose async source cancellation/KV promise lifetime independently of HTTP; do not blame the HTTP ingress from absent observations alone.

A Workerd patch or package upgrade requires a pinned candidate, independent reproducible runtime source/build provenance and the unchanged original strict suite passing; open upstream PRs are not proof.
